name: Time, Money & Entropy
essence: A function that consults wall-clock time or money in floats answers differently every call.

examples.summary: Currency summed as float64 fails an exact equality check.
examples.mechanism: 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 have no exact binary representation; error accumulates (CWE-1339).

examples.summary: Date and hour come from two clock reads; across midnight the key mixes the old date with the new hour.
examples.mechanism: Each `clock()` call is a fresh hidden input; one logical instant should be read once.

examples.summary: `==` on time.Time compares monotonic reading and location pointer, not the instant.
examples.mechanism: `time.Now()` carries a monotonic clock reading that Parse drops; use `Equal`.

examples.summary: Repeated f64 deposits of 0.10 never equal 1.00.
examples.mechanism: Binary floating point accumulates representation error (CWE-1339).

examples.summary: `as_secs()` truncates sub-second durations to 0, then divides by it.
examples.mechanism: Wall-clock-derived value is an untrusted hidden input; truncation turns it into zero.

examples.summary: Integer division splits 1000 cents into three 333s, losing a cent.
examples.mechanism: Truncating division discards the remainder instead of distributing it (CWE-682).

examples.summary: Dollar amounts as JS numbers: 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3, so an exact payment is reported short.
examples.mechanism: IEEE-754 doubles cannot represent decimal money exactly.

examples.summary: Adding one month to Jan 31 overflows Feb and lands on Mar 3.
examples.mechanism: `setUTCMonth` keeps the day-of-month and rolls excess days forward.

examples.summary: `trialEnd` mutates the Date passed in, so the stored trial start moves to the end date.
examples.mechanism: Date objects are mutable and passed by reference.

examples.summary: Experiment variant is drawn from Math.random per view, so one user sees both variants.
examples.mechanism: Assignment should be a deterministic function of userId (CWE-330).

examples.summary: Creation and expiry timestamps come from separate `Date.now()` reads, so the hold window drifts.
examples.mechanism: Time elapses between reads; capture `now` once per transaction.

examples.summary: Ten dimes added as binary floats do not equal one dollar.
examples.mechanism: 0.1 has no exact float representation, so the sum lands just under 1.

examples.summary: The date is taken from 23:59:59 and the hour from the next midnight, so the key says hour 00.
examples.mechanism: Two separate clock reads can fall on different days. One snapshot would keep date and hour together.

examples.summary: The same seeded draw sends one visitor to control and the next to trial.
examples.mechanism: random.random reads and advances the module generator, so two calls in one run are not the same branch.
examples.expected_behavior: both visitors on the same branch

examples.summary: Half-cent amounts round to the even integer: 0, 2, and 2.
examples.mechanism: round uses banker's rounding. 0.5 goes to 0 and 2.5 goes to 2.

examples.summary: Adding 30 days to January 31 lands on March 2, not February 28 or March 1.
examples.mechanism: timedelta counts days. It does not clamp to the last day of the next month.
